To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the complex structure of the compactification manifold is stabilized by RR fluxes and the stabilization is achieved without orientifold projection.
the complex structure fields can be stabilized at a supersymmetric minimum with no need of a non-vanishing NS flux.

we have derived stability conditions for the no-scale scalar potentials governing the dynamics of complex structure moduli in Calabi–Yav compactifications and non-geometric ones, and that we have shown that in the non-geometric case it is possible to stabilize the moduli at weak coupling, with no need of an orientifold projection, but possibly with the need of breaking supersymmetry.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the stabilization of all the moduli at weak coupling requires the presence of H RR flux, and the breaking of supersymmetry, while the presence of HNS flux or corrections to scalar potential are not necessary.

the stabilization of the complex structure fields at weak string coupling is possible in the presence of either NSNS, R-R or non-geometric fluxes, but the stabilization of the axio-dilation and the stabilization at strong coupling requires supersymmetry breaking.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown the possibility of obtaining a no-scale structure in type IIB compactifications with non-geometric flux.
the stabilization of the complex structure fields in terms of H R only is a necessary but not a sufficient condition for the stabilization of the whole scalar sector.
the no-scale potential is not only a useful tool to study compactifications of type II theories, but it is also a very useful tool to study non-geometric compactifications.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the no-scale structure of the scalar potential is preserved even when one allows for the presence of H RR fluxes.
the existence of a metastable de Sitter space in the string landscape may be compatible with the absence of a non-perturbative superpotential and of an orientifold projection.

the no-scale structure of the scalar potential, which is a feature of the rigid Calabi– Yau limit, is preserved in the non-geometric background, thus suggesting that the stabilization mechanism may be a generic feature of string compactifications.
